findings.title: Per-request ssl_context overrides subclass init_poolmanager TLS settings
findings.suggested_fix:
In `HTTPAdapter._get_connection`, after computing `pool_kwargs` and selecting the manager (`self.poolmanager` or the proxy manager), skip the shared context if the manager carries its own TLS settings:

```python
manager = proxy_manager if proxy else self.poolmanager
if pool_kwargs.get("ssl_context") is _preloaded_ssl_context and any(
    k in manager.connection_pool_kw
    for k in ("ssl_context", "ssl_version", "ssl_minimum_version", "ssl_maximum_version", "ca_certs", "ca_cert_dir", "ca_cert_data")
):
    del pool_kwargs["ssl_context"]
    pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)
```

Assumption: subclasses that override `init_poolmanager` still assign `self.poolmanager` (as the docs example does), so `connection_pool_kw` is inspectable.
findings.first_evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:94-95: `elif verify is True:` / `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context`

findings.title: http URL via https proxy now raises ValueError (verify=True)
findings.suggested_fix:
Only attach the shared context for https request URLs, mirroring `cert_verify()`'s `url.lower().startswith("https")` guard:

```python
elif verify is True:
    if scheme == "https":
        pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context
```

(`scheme` is already computed at line 89.) For direct http requests urllib3 strips SSL kwargs anyway (poolmanager.py:277-279), so this only changes the https-proxy forwarding leg, which `cert_verify()` already marks CERT_NONE as before.
findings.first_evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:95: `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context` (no check on `scheme`) and src/requests/adapters.py:318-319: `else: conn.cert_reqs = "CERT_NONE"` for non-https URLs

findings.title: HTTPS-proxy TLS trust silently switches from certifi to OS store
findings.suggested_fix: In `HTTPAdapter._get_connection`, when `proxy_url.scheme == "https"` and `verify is True`, also set `pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` so `_connect_tls_proxy` keeps loading certifi for the proxy leg (this reintroduces one `load_verify_locations()` per connection for https-proxy users only). Alternatively construct the https `ProxyManager` with `proxy_ssl_context=_preloaded_ssl_context`, but note that makes proxy verification independent of `verify=False`, which is a behaviour change in the other direction, hence a design decision.
findings.first_evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:304-317: `if verify is not True:` ... `conn.ca_certs = cert_loc` -- `ca_certs` is now only set for string `verify`; merge-base set `conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` for verify=True

findings.title: Import of requests now fails if certifi bundle is unreadable
findings.suggested_fix:
Build the context lazily and keep the existence check:

```python
_preloaded_ssl_context = None

def _get_preloaded_ssl_context():
    global _preloaded_ssl_context
    if _preloaded_ssl_context is None:
        cert_loc = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)
        if not cert_loc or not os.path.exists(cert_loc):
            raise OSError(f"Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, invalid path: {cert_loc}")
        ctx = create_urllib3_context()
        ctx.load_verify_locations(cert_loc)
        _preloaded_ssl_context = ctx
    return _preloaded_ssl_context
```

and call it from `_urllib3_request_context`. Guard with a lock if first-use races matter (a duplicate build is harmless).
findings.first_evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:75-78: `_preloaded_ssl_context = create_urllib3_context()` / `_preloaded_ssl_context.load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))` at module scope

residual_risks: Thread-safety of the shared SSL_CTX: urllib3 performs `context.verify_mode = ...` (connection.py:1042) and `context.set_alpn_protocols(...)` (ssl_.py:435) on the shared context for every connection from every thread while other threads are mid-handshake; urllib3 applies the same pattern to user-supplied contexts so it is probably tolerated by OpenSSL, but it was not verified here and the PR's motivating workload is 30 concurrent threads.

urllib3 1.26.x is not installed; all library traces are against 2.8.0. From memory, 1.26's `ssl_wrap_socket` also calls `load_cert_chain` on a supplied context and `HTTPSConnection.connect` also assigns `context.verify_mode`, so findings 1 and 3 are expected to hold there too, unverified.

pyOpenSSL injection after `import requests` leaves the shared context as a stdlib `ssl.SSLContext`; urllib3 then sets `check_hostname = False` on it permanently (connection.py:1056) and relies on its own `_match_hostname`; no verification loss identified, but the mutated flag persists across later un-injection.

Test failure `test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings` is attributable to fixture age, not this diff: tests/certs/mtls/client/client.pem was generated with `-days 730` and committed 2024-03-14 (a94e9b53), so it expired around 2026-03-14; the failing first request is `verify=False` which never touches the new context. Note the test's second request (`verify=True` + `cert`) is the in-repo path for finding 1.
callsite completeness: grep-only for third-party `HTTPAdapter` subclasses that pass TLS settings via `init_poolmanager`/`proxy_manager_for`; external usage cannot be enumerated from this repo.
testing_gaps: No test asserts the optimisation itself: e.g. patch `ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations` and assert it is not called for a `verify=True` request after import.

No test for `verify=True` + `cert=` followed by a `verify=True` request without `cert` (same or different Session) asserting no client certificate is presented; the existing mTLS test only checks the first request with `verify=False`.
No test for an `HTTPAdapter` subclass passing `ssl_context`/`ssl_minimum_version` via `init_poolmanager` with `verify=True`, asserting the subclass context is the one used.
No test for an `http://` URL through an `https://` proxy with `verify=True`, nor for the trust store used on the https-proxy TLS leg.

findings.suggested_fix: Add two tests in TestPreparingURLs. (1) Pool-key contract: `host_params, pool_kwargs = requests.adapters._urllib3_request_context(req, True, None)`; assert `pool_kwargs == {"ssl_context": requests.adapters._preloaded_ssl_context, "cert_reqs": "CERT_REQUIRED"}` and that `"ca_certs"`/`"ca_cert_dir"` are absent. (2) Positive handshake: with `TLSServer(cert_chain="tests/certs/valid/server/server.pem", keyfile="tests/certs/valid/server/server.key")`, build `ctx = create_urllib3_context(); ctx.load_verify_locations("tests/certs/valid/ca/ca.crt")`, `monkeypatch.setattr(requests.adapters, "_preloaded_ssl_context", ctx)`, then assert `requests.Session().get(url).status_code == 200` (no `verify=` argument) and that `s.get(url, verify=False)` plus `s.get(url)` yield 2 pools. The positive case fails if the context is not actually used for verification or if the connection reloads/overrides the trust store.

If maintainers prefer, exposing the context via a small factory (e.g. `_default_ssl_context()` with `functools.lru_cache`) would make the suggested tests less brittle; not raised as a finding because it is a design choice.
testing_gaps: Import-time failure mode: the diff removes the request-time `OSError("Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle...")` for the default bundle (old cert_verify) and instead calls `load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))` at `import requests.adapters` (src/requests/adapters.py:76-78). A test that monkeypatches `DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH` cannot cover this because loading has already happened at import.

No test asserts that `verify=True` and `verify="tests/certs/valid/ca/ca.crt"` select different pools, which is the case that now depends on `key_ssl_context` versus `key_ca_certs` differing.

findings.suggested_fix:
In `HTTPAdapter._get_connection`, after resolving the manager (`self.poolmanager` or the `ProxyManager`), drop the shared context when the manager was configured with any TLS kwargs and fall back to the old per-pool bundle:

```python
manager = proxy_manager if proxy else self.poolmanager
if pool_kwargs.get("ssl_context") is _preloaded_ssl_context and any(
    k in manager.connection_pool_kw for k in (
        "ssl_context", "ssl_version", "ssl_minimum_version", "ssl_maximum_version",

    del pool_kwargs["ssl_context"]
    pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)
```

and set `conn.ca_certs` accordingly in `cert_verify` for that case. Assumes subclasses use `init_poolmanager`/`proxy_manager_for` kwargs (the documented surface).

findings.title: import requests now fails when the certifi bundle is missing or unreadable
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace the module-level construction with a lazily built singleton:

```python
_preloaded_ssl_context = None
_preloaded_ssl_context_lock = threading.Lock()

def _get_preloaded_ssl_context():
    global _preloaded_ssl_context
    if _preloaded_ssl_context is None:
        with _preloaded_ssl_context_lock:
            if _preloaded_ssl_context is None:
                cert_loc = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)
                if not cert_loc or not os.path.exists(cert_loc):
                    raise OSError(f"Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, invalid path: {cert_loc}")
                ctx = create_urllib3_context()
                ctx.load_verify_locations(cert_loc)
                _preloaded_ssl_context = ctx
    return _preloaded_ssl_context
```

and call it from `_urllib3_request_context` in the `verify is True` branch.

residual_risks: Thread-safety of mutating one ssl.SSLContext while other threads call wrap_socket() on it: every connect now runs context.set_alpn_protocols(...) (urllib3/util/ssl_.py:435), context.verify_mode = ... (connection.py:1042) and possibly load_cert_chain on the shared object; OpenSSL does not guarantee SSL_CTX mutation concurrent with SSL_new. Could not verify CPython GIL coverage from source in this environment (read-only, compiled _ssl).

urllib3 1.26.x is not installed; findings were traced on 2.8.0. In 1.26 ssl_wrap_socket also calls load_verify_locations/load_cert_chain on the supplied context and _connect_tls_proxy also falls back to load_default_certs, so the same conclusions are expected but unverified.

residual_risks: Shared-context mutation per handshake: urllib3 writes `context.verify_mode = ...` (urllib3/connection.py:1042) and `context.set_alpn_protocols(ALPN_PROTOCOLS)` (urllib3/util/ssl_.py:435) on the shared `_preloaded_ssl_context` for every new connection in every thread. OpenSSL's SSL_CTX_set_alpn_protos frees and replaces ctx->ext.alpn without a lock while SSL_new (called by CPython with the GIL released) copies it; the writes are cheap (no measurable perf cost) but the pattern is a theoretical cross-thread data race that did not exist when each connection had a private context. Not raised as a finding because CPython/OpenSSL sources are not available here to quote.

findings.title: Per-request bundle OSError becomes import-time crash
findings.suggested_fix:
Build the context lazily and keep the old error surface:

```python
import threading
_preloaded_ssl_context = None
_preloaded_ssl_context_lock = threading.Lock()

def _get_preloaded_ssl_context():
    global _preloaded_ssl_context
    if _preloaded_ssl_context is None:
        with _preloaded_ssl_context_lock:
            if _preloaded_ssl_context is None:
                cert_loc = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)
                if not cert_loc or not os.path.exists(cert_loc):
                    raise OSError(
                        f"Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, "
                        f"invalid path: {cert_loc}"
                    )
                ctx = create_urllib3_context()
                ctx.load_verify_locations(cert_loc)
                _preloaded_ssl_context = ctx
    return _preloaded_ssl_context
```

and use `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _get_preloaded_ssl_context()` in `_urllib3_request_context`. `ssl.SSLError` from a malformed bundle is an `OSError` subclass, so the exception type callers already handle is preserved. Add a test that monkeypatches `DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH` to a nonexistent path and asserts an `https` `verify=True` request raises `OSError` while `verify=False` / `verify=<path>` requests still work.

findings.title: Preloaded context silently overrides subclass TLS pool settings
findings.suggested_fix:
Decide in `_get_connection` (which has access to the adapter) rather than in the module-level helper. After `host_params, pool_kwargs = _urllib3_request_context(...)`, add:

```python
        base_kw = self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw
        if pool_kwargs.get("ssl_context") is _preloaded_ssl_context and any(
            k in base_kw
            for k in ("ssl_context", "ssl_version", "ssl_minimum_version",
                      "ssl_maximum_version", "ca_certs", "ca_cert_dir", "ca_cert_data")
        ):
            # Adapter supplies its own TLS configuration; do not clobber it.
            del pool_kwargs["ssl_context"]
```

and in `cert_verify` restore the pre-diff `conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` for `verify is True` when `conn.ssl_context is not _preloaded_ssl_context` (so the subclass's context still gets the certifi bundle loaded per connection, exactly as before). Apply the same check for proxy managers (`self.proxy_manager[proxy].connection_pool_kw`). Add a test with an `HTTPAdapter` subclass whose `init_poolmanager` passes `ssl_context=ctx` and assert the pool created for a `verify=True` request uses `ctx`.
